solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: False rumours stop women leaving hospital units

parts.note: to can something is to stop or put an end to it

indicators.note: women leaving the units means that letter departs from the word

parts.note: wards are the units of a hospital

explanation.surface: Untrue gossip puts a halt to the sight of female staff walking out of the wards.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded story or hoax spread about, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Acres have the capacity, so plant

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acres
can means be able to
thus means so or therefore

explanation.surface: Acres of land are big enough to grow something.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian column carving.

clue.text: College has a couple of lines on alarm about University lecturer

parts.note: L is a line, so two of them give LL

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the distress call goes round the other letters

parts.note: SOS is a distress call raising the alarm

explanation.surface: A college writes a few lines on an alarm concerning one of its academics.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL SOULS is an Oxford college with no undergraduates.
explanation.definitionFit: All Souls is a famous college of Oxford University.

clue.text: Extinct group unexpectedly is around, I initially admitted

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning up out of order, so the letters are scrambled
initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A vanished group turns up surprisingly, and one person confesses first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' scrambles IS AROUND, I and A, the first letter of 'admitted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosauria is the scientific name of the class of prehistoric reptiles that died out.

clue.text: Try to show courage, lacking character in the end

indicators.note: lacking the character at the end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: heart means courage, as in take heart

explanation.surface: An attempt to be brave that falters at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense, not attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who hears a case tries it in court.

clue.text: Gloomy — short time, then uplifted

parts.note: mo is short for moment
rose means went up

explanation.surface: Briefly down, then cheered up.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy in temperament.

clue.text: Quantity of water from river filling cup

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so one letter sits within the other word

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking cup

explanation.surface: Pouring water from a river into a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quantity of water' suggests a measure in the cup; it is a wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaker is a large wave crashing on the shore, a mass of seawater.

clue.text: Build with no hint of reliability? It's about time for law

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shortened word goes around the letter
with no means a letter is removed

parts.note: stature means build or physique

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Construction without reliability needs a timely legal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping R from STATURE gives STATUE, which goes 'about' T.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Revolutionary comrade beginning to taunt US politician

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so the letters of comrade are reordered
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A firebrand comrade starts to mock an American member of Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as an adjective for the comrade but signals the anagram of COMRADE into DEMOCRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of one of the two main American parties are known by this name.

clue.text: Following behind, having taken front off fence

indicators.note: taking the front off a word removes its opening letter

parts.note: trailing means following behind someone

explanation.surface: Someone trails another and decapitates the fence on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a barrier of posts and rails, a kind of fence.

clue.text: Organ playing in display of skill that's high-handed

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: art is skill shown in performance

indicators.note: the organ playing suggests its letters being set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: An organist shows off in a performance that comes across as overbearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals the anagram; 'that's' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone acting with haughty, overbearing superiority.

clue.text: Period in December not initially certain to provide exciting event

parts.note: Advent is the church season before Christmas, running through December

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is removed

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A December season promises uncertain excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a thrilling or daring experience.

clue.text: Football and rugby, say, tossed around these leather items

indicators.note: tossed around suggests the word turned to face the other way

parts.note: football and rugby are examples of sports

explanation.surface: Balls in two games are thrown about near some leather goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed around' turns SPORTS end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Strops are leather straps used to sharpen razors.

clue.text: US lawyer rejected version of events I'm giving US counsel

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor throws out a witness's account while offering legal advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges EVENTS and I'M into VISEMENT; 'rejected' turns DA into AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Advisement is American usage for advice or careful consideration, as in taking a matter under advisement.

clue.text: Horse-drawn carriage and boat displayed with theatrical skill

parts.note: a stage is short for stagecoach
a craft is a boat or vessel

explanation.surface: A coach and a boat are put on show with dramatic flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagecraft is the art of writing or staging plays.

clue.text: Yank to have success with girl

definitions.meaning: a yank is a sharp tug
slang for attracting someone romantically on a night out

explanation.surface: An American hopes to charm a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb meaning tug.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are one verb: tug hard, and in British slang win someone over romantically.

clue.text: Wise man accepting hard quantity of ice will show loss of size

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word holds the others

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a rink is a sheet of ice for skating

explanation.surface: A wise person takes hard ice and sees it melt away.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the amount by which something contracts or becomes smaller.

clue.text: He copies bird's Latin listing — that will be shown up

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: shown up in a down clue means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A mimic copies a bird's Latin list, which then gets exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' reverses ROTA into ATOR, as the clue is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An emulator is someone who imitates or tries to equal another.

clue.text: Unanimous description of how two halfwits could appear?

definitions.text: description of how two halfwits could appear?
definitions.meaning: two halves of a person put together make a single whole person

explanation.surface: Two dimwits appear to agree completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: two half-wits, as halves, would together look like a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together with one accord, everyone in complete agreement.

clue.text: Doctor is cross making cut

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: An angry doctor makes an incision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To scissor is to cut with shears.

clue.text: Pupil, say, given place in professional squad, not amateur

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: given a place in means put inside the other word
not means the following letters are removed

parts.note: a team is a squad of players
AM is the abbreviation for amateur
EG means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A student gets a spot in a professional team, beating the amateurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for EG (for example); 'Pupil, say' looks like the definition but only 'Pupil' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone guided and promoted by a mentor.

clue.text: Confusion occurring in Times sometimes

indicators.note: the letters occur inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A newspaper occasionally prints muddled material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occurring in' points to letters spanning 'Times sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of disorder or muddle.

clue.text: Polluted air: guy involved in treatment exaggerated picture

indicators.note: being involved in something puts these letters inside it

parts.note: a cure is a course of medical treatment

indicators.note: polluted air is spoilt, so its letters are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: cat is old slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Dirty air means a man ends up in medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polluted' gives ARI; 'guy' is old slang for a man, here a cat as in jazz talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature is a drawing that exaggerates features for comic effect.

clue.text: Wrong to block firm with European function

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in between, so the word goes inside

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing gets in the way of a European company's business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like an office duty but is mathematical.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosine is a trigonometric function of an angle.

clue.text: It's settled: stop completion of motorway

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark, a kind of stop

indicators.note: the completion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A decision has been reached to halt work on finishing a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's settled' reads as 'decided' but means a place that has been settled by incomers.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a territory occupied by settlers from elsewhere.

clue.text: Determined whisper not given any credence?

parts.note: set means fixed or determined
an aside is a remark spoken quietly so others do not hear

explanation.surface: A firm murmur that nobody believes.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside a claim or ruling is to disregard or dismiss it.

clue.text: Platform reputed to have ends switched

indicators.note: switching the ends means the first and last letters change places

parts.note: said means reputed, as in the said person

explanation.surface: A stage rumoured to be turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: SAID with S and D exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform in a hall.

clue.text: I'm covered in glue as a result of hobby

indicators.note: being covered in something puts these letters inside it

parts.note: paste is a soft adhesive
I'm gives I and M

explanation.surface: Someone sticky with glue blames their hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is an activity done for enjoyment in spare hours.

clue.text: Newspaper, say, to cease providing material

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group, a newspaper for example
to die is to stop or come to an end

explanation.surface: A newspaper is about to fold, ending its supply of content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like copy for a newspaper but means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff cotton fabric.

clue.text: Keeping nothing wrapped in cord

indicators.note: wrapped in puts the small piece inside the other

parts.note: string is thin cord
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Holding on to an empty package tied with cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Storing something means keeping it for later use.
